evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/core.tsx:99-101 — the Home page 'Open dashboard' button routes with an exact-equality role check: `navigate(user?.role === 'manager' ? '/dashboard/manager' : '/dashboard/resident')`. This sends EVERY manager-equivalent role other than the bare 'manager' string — `org_admin`, `super_admin`, `technical_manager`, `property_manager` — to the RESIDENT dashboard instead of the manager dashboard.

The repo already has the single-source-of-truth helper `isManagerRole(role)` in routes/shared.tsx:48 (backed by `MANAGER_ROLES = ['manager','org_admin','super_admin','technical_manager','property_manager']`), and it is used elsewhere precisely to avoid this drift: App.tsx:127 `const isOperator = isManagerRole(user?.role)` gates the operator nav links, and the detail/workspace route wrappers gate on it too. Home's hand-rolled `=== 'manager'` is the outlier and contradicts that helper — an org_admin sees operator-only nav links (App.tsx) but the Home CTA drops them onto the resident dashboard.

Impact: MEDIUM — role-based mis-routing / UX-correctness for all non-'manager' operator roles (the most common operator role in a seeded org is typically org_admin, so this likely mis-routes the majority of operators). Fix: `navigate(isManagerRole(user?.role) ? '/dashboard/manager' : '/dashboard/resident')`, importing `isManagerRole` from '../shared' (already imported in this module's sibling files). Confidence medium: the wrong branch is confirmed by static read; the resident dashboard is still a reachable page so this is a correctness/UX defect rather than a crash.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/core.tsx:166-168 — the dashboard routes register `/dashboard/manager` -> <ManagerDashboardPage/> and `/dashboard/resident` -> <ResidentDashboardPage/> with NO <ProtectedRoute> wrapper, and :166 redirects bare `/dashboard` -> `/dashboard/manager` for everyone. Contrast the immediately-following `/dashboard/customize` route (:171-178) which IS wrapped `<ProtectedRoute requiredRoles={['org_admin','super_admin']}>`, and every /settings/* route in settingsRoutes() which is wrapped in <ProtectedRoute>.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/dashboard/pages/ManagerDashboardPage.tsx:21-49 — the page does NOT self-guard: it has no `if (!isAuthenticated) return <Navigate to="/login"/>` (unlike the auth/profile pages ProfileEditPage/ChangePasswordPage/TwoFactorAuthPage which do), and its only role use is `canCustomize` (:27-28, gating a customize LINK for org_admin/super_admin). Per its own header doc it 'never gates on layout fetch — falls back to DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_LAYOUT on error or while loading' (:3-5, :43), so the manager dashboard shell renders even with no/failed data.

Consequence: (a) an UNAUTHENTICATED visitor hitting /dashboard or /dashboard/manager by URL renders the full manager dashboard shell (nav + default layout) instead of being bounced to /login — a broken-access-control / info-disclosure smell for the operator surface; (b) any RESIDENT is actively redirected by :166 (/dashboard -> /dashboard/manager) into the manager dashboard. The underlying API data is backend-RLS-protected (queries will 403/empty), so this leaks the manager UI shell/structure rather than tenant data — but it is inconsistent with the app's own ProtectedRoute convention and the self-guard pattern used by every other auth-sensitive page.

Impact: MEDIUM — authorization-completeness / access-control consistency. Fix: wrap `/dashboard/manager` (and `/dashboard/resident`) in <ProtectedRoute> (manager route additionally `requiredRoles={[...MANAGER_ROLES]}` so residents land on the resident dashboard, aligning with finding code-review-ppt-web-core-home-dashboard-role-route), OR add an isAuthenticated/role self-guard to ManagerDashboardPage mirroring the auth pages. Confidence medium: missing wrappers + missing self-guard confirmed by static read; the practical severity is bounded by backend RLS on the data, hence not HIGH.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/App.tsx:135 — the primary navigation landmark uses a HARDCODED English accessibility label: `<nav className="app-nav" aria-label="Main navigation">`. This is a user-facing (screen-reader) string not wrapped in `t()`, so it stays English for all locales (the app ships sk/cs/de/en per root CLAUDE.md and this SPA uses react-i18next).

It is inconsistent with the sibling aria-labels in the very same component that ARE localized: App.tsx:178 `aria-label={t('auth.signOut', { defaultValue: 'Sign out' })}`. Every visible nav link in AppNavigation is already routed through `t(...)` (:136-190); only the landmark's aria-label was missed.

Impact: LOW — i18n/a11y gap on a single landmark label (screen-reader users on non-English locales hear an English region name). Fix: `aria-label={t('nav.mainNavigation', { defaultValue: 'Main navigation' })}` and add the key to the i18n bundles. Confidence medium: the hardcoded literal is confirmed by static read; classified LOW per the skill's i18n-gap tier.
